title: Form catalog — gateable forms
preamble:
# Form catalog — construct capabilities

The catalog of the construct capabilities that gate a
surface construct: the subset of DS language features a
program's settings can permit or forbid. Every capability
here represents something a tier might not have. Setting
one `false` means "rules on this tier don't have access to
this construct," and the compiler refuses programs that use
it. The registry of every capability is [LCAP].

The BNF does not change with any setting. Settings restrict
constructs, not the grammar: rule authors always read and
write the same syntax; only the available constructs vary.

Non-gateable language features — expression grammar,
pattern matching, schema and rule declarations, truth
maintenance, interpolation, the
`emit` / `log` action surface, adapter dotted
sugar, `within` / `dwell` temporal predicates,
synthetic-identifier reservation, fact-category markers —
are **simply part of the language**. They're covered by
[LGRA] as the normative source and
inventoried at [LLSU]
as a cross-check.

## What this is not

- Not a full language feature inventory. See [LLSU].
- Not a subset-language definition. One BNF regardless of
  settings. Gating is compile-time validation against the
  program's settings, not parser variation.
- Not a vehicle for tier authors to invent their own
  dialects of DS. The expressive surface a rule author
  writes against is the same everywhere; what differs is
  which capabilities the runtime provides to that tier's
  rules.
